subject: prediction from zero-inflated negative binomial regression

messages.author: 09ad8d237e8d8786
messages.subject: prediction from zero-inflated negative binomial regression
parts:
Dear Group,

I ran a zero-inflated negative binomial regression using the multiple likelihood facility. Please see my code with the attached simulated data.

cruise2 <- read.csv(file="cruise_tr1.csv",head=T)

z <- cruise2$count>0 +0
y <- ifelse(cruise2$count>0,cruise2$count,NA)
stk.z <- inla.stack(tag='est.z',
                    data=list(Y=cbind(z,NA)),
                    A=list(1),
                    effects=list(list(z.b0=rep(1,length(z)),
                                      DEPTH.z=cruise2$DEPTH,
                                      dist.z=cruise2$dist)))
stk.y <- inla.stack(tag='est.y',
                    data=list(Y=cbind(NA,y)),
                    A=list(1),
                    effects=list(list(y.b0=rep(1,length(y)),
                                      DEPTH.y=cruise2$DEPTH,
                                      dist.y=cruise2$dist)))
stk.zy <- inla.stack(stk.z,stk.y)
formula2 <- Y ~ 0+z.b0+ DEPTH.z +  dist.z  + y.b0 + DEPTH.y +  dist.y
result.zinb <- inla(formula2,family=c("binomial","nbinomial"),
                    data=inla.stack.data(stk.zy),
                    control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stk.zy),quantiles=NULL),
                    control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),verbose=TRUE,
                    control.fixed = list(expand.factor.strategy='inla'))
summary(result.zinb)

But I can not figure out a way to generate prediction from the model,

fit <- result.zinb$summary.fitted.values[,"mean"]
lpred <-  result.zinb$summary.linear.predictor[,"mean"]
dim(lpred) <- c(length(y),4)
dim(fit) <- c(length(y),4)
summary(fit[,1]-binomial()$linkinv(lpred[,1]))

The first column of summary.fitted.values seems to be the probability of binomial distribution, but is it possible to calculate predictive values from the model?

Regards
dong

How 'fitted values' works is described here.

http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-How-can-I-do-predictions-using-INLA-


in particular, you must supply an argument 'link' which say who is who
when it comes to link functions used. 

the link functions are also available with INLA, like

> inla.link.
inla.link.cauchit      inla.link.invcauchit   inla.link.invlogit     in
la.link.log          inla.link.tan
inla.link.cloglog      inla.link.invcloglog   inla.link.invloglog    in
la.link.logit        
inla.link.identity     inla.link.invidentity  inla.link.invprobit    in
la.link.loglog       
inla.link.invalid      inla.link.invlog       inla.link.invtan       in
la.link.probit       
> inla.link.

## fit a zero-inflated negative binomial regression with count data

stk.z <- inla.stack(tag='est.z',
                    data=list(Y=cbind(z,NA)),
                    A=list(1),
                    effects=list(list(z.b0=rep(1,length(z)),
                                      DEPTH.z=cruise2$DEPTH,
                                      dist.z=cruise2$dist)))
stk.y <- inla.stack(tag='est.y',
                    data=list(Y=cbind(NA,y)),
                    A=list(1),
                    effects=list(list(y.b0=rep(1,length(y)),
                                      DEPTH.y=cruise2$DEPTH,
                                      dist.y=cruise2$dist)))
stk.zy <- inla.stack(stk.z,stk.y)
formula2 <- Y ~ 0+z.b0+ DEPTH.z +  dist.z  + y.b0 + DEPTH.y +  dist.y

result.zinb <- inla(formula2,family=c("binomial","zeroinflatednbinomial0"),
                    data=inla.stack.data(stk.zy),
                    control.family=list(
                      list(),
                      list(hyper=list(prob=list(initial=-20,fixed=TRUE)))),
                    control.predictor=list(link=link,A=inla.stack.A(stk.zy),quantiles=NULL),

sd <- result.zinb$summary.fitted.values[,"sd"]
dim(sd) <- dim(fit) <- c(length(y),4)
## predictive mean
summary(fit[,1] * fit[,2])
## predictive standard error
summary(sqrt(fit[,1] * (fit[,2]^2+sd[,2]^2)))
